notes: Behavioral evals for the dev-log-backfill skill. Each targets a place a generic agent would default the wrong way: skipping the existing-entries check, fabricating a confident 'why' from terse commits, dumping one entry per commit on a huge repo, or posting before Matt has reviewed the drafts. Run a fresh agent that reads SKILL.md (not the evals) per prompt, then grade the output against the expectations.

evals.name: basic-backfill-trigger
evals.prompt: This repo doesn't have any dev log yet — can you backfill one from the git history?
evals.expected_output: Pulls the full git history, checks Basecamp for existing dev log entries first, groups commits into dated/thematic entries, drafts them in the standard dev-log format, and shows the drafts before posting anything.
expectations: Pulls the full git history (e.g. `git log --oneline` or `--format=... --date=short`) rather than guessing at past work
Checks Basecamp for existing "Dev log —" messages before drafting, so it doesn't duplicate real-time entries
Groups commits by date/theme rather than listing every commit individually
Drafts entries in the "Dev log — YYYY-MM-DD: summary" title format with categorized Markdown bullets
Shows the drafted entries and waits for confirmation before posting anything to Basecamp

evals.name: terse-commits-no-fabrication
evals.prompt: Backfill the dev log for this repo. Most of the commit messages are just 'wip', 'fix', or 'more work' — there's not much to go on.
evals.expected_output: Acknowledges the git history is terse, sticks to describing what changed rather than inventing motivations it can't infer, and flags which entries are guesses.
expectations: Does not invent a confident "why" for commits where the message and diff don't support one
Falls back to describing what changed when the reasoning can't be inferred, rather than fabricating narrative
Is upfront that terse commit history makes the entries less narrative-rich than real-time ones
Flags any inferred/uncertain reasoning to the reader rather than presenting guesses as fact

evals.name: existing-entries-no-duplicate
evals.prompt: Backfill the dev log — but heads up, we started posting dev logs about a month ago, so there's already some entries on the message board.
evals.expected_output: Checks the existing dev log messages first and only backfills commit history from before the earliest existing entry, rather than re-covering already-logged work.
expectations: Explicitly checks for existing "Dev log —" messages on the project's message board before drafting
Scopes the backfill to dates before the earliest existing real-time entry
Does not attempt to edit or overwrite the existing entries
Avoids re-summarizing work the existing entries already cover

evals.name: large-old-repo-density
evals.prompt: This repo is almost 2 years old with a huge commit history. Can you backfill a dev log for the whole thing?
evals.expected_output: Groups the history into a readable narrative of milestones instead of one entry per day or commit, explicitly favoring density over completeness for a repo this size.
expectations: Does not attempt one entry per day or per commit for a 2-year history
Groups related work into meaningful milestones or date ranges
Skips or folds in trivial-commit days (typos, merges, version bumps) rather than giving them their own entry
Reflects the "density over completeness" framing when explaining the approach
